page.summary: The web app (apps/web) is a Next.js 16 App Router site plus the server API (apps/web/app/api) that every other app and third parties call. It hosts Cloud chat, accounts, billing, admin and marketing pages, and it is the UI the public Electron desktop loads. Sign-in is Clerk behind an identity port. Web is Cloud-only (Free and paid plans); Local runs only inside the Electron host; BYOK is not on web.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `apps/web` is two things in one deployable: (1) the Next.js web application (marketing pages, sign-in, chat, projects, artifacts, settings, billing, admin) and (2) the server API under `apps/web/app/api` (88 top-level route folders) that Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and third parties call. [code] (apps/web/app/api; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:29 describes the API as 'the HTTP surface under apps/web/app/api that the other six and third parties call').

**Users.**
- Visitors: public marketing, legal, help, pricing and download pages. [code] (apps/web/app)
- Signed-in Free users: managed Cloud chat on the Free plan. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:323, `free` is in `CLOUD_CHAT_TIERS`)
- Subscribed users: the same chat plus paid capabilities (connectors, deep research, image and video generation, developer surfaces, team admin). [code] (billing-catalog.ts:346-361)
- Admins and workspace owners: `apps/web/app/admin`, `apps/web/features/admin`, `apps/web/features/workspace-console`.
- Guests: a small anonymous chat route exists, off unless a feature flag is on. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest/route.ts; apps/web/lib/guest-chat/guest-chat-access.ts)
- Public Electron Desktop users: the Electron window shows the hosted web app, so they use web UI. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md, 'The desktop is two shells'; docs/architecture/overview.md 'Public Electron Desktop uses the hosted web settings surface')

**Role in the product.** suite.md names Web as: account, projects, synced app chats, artifacts, admin, Free managed access, and the owner of waitlist/access-code-gated paid acquisition. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:31)

**Published state label.** The website marks only Web as 'Available now'; Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome read 'Coming soon'. [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13)

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
| Layer | Choice | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framework | Next.js 16, App Router, React 19 | [code] (apps/web/package.json: next ^16.4.5, react 19.3.0; ARCHITECTURE.md Surfaces table) |
| Routing middleware | `apps/web/proxy.ts` exporting `proxy` (not `middleware.ts`) | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5); [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts) |
| Identity | Clerk (`@clerk/nextjs`) behind an `IdentityProvider` port; default provider name `clerk`, chosen by env `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:9-11; apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts) |
| Database | Neon Postgres via `@neondatabase/serverless` and `@agiworkforce/data-layer`; migrations in `apps/web/db/neon` (577 entries in the folder) | [code] (apps/web/package.json; apps/web/db/neon) |
| Payments | Stripe (checkout route); Apple store library also a dependency (mobile IAP route `apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap`) | [code] (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts; package.json `@apple/app-store-server-library`) |
| Storage | S3-compatible object storage (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `@agiworkforce/object-storage`) | [code] (package.json) |
| Code sandbox | `@e2b/code-interpreter` | [code] (package.json) |
| Providers | One adapter per provider under `packages/ai/providers/*` (anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, groq, minimax, moonshot, nvidia, ollama, lmstudio, openrouter, perplexity, qwen, zhipu, workers-ai, vercel-gateway, factory); web also depends on `@agiworkforce/provider-runtime`, `providers-factory`, `providers-vercel-gateway`, `routing` | [code] (ls packages/ai/providers; apps/web/package.json) |
| Models | Not written in web code; the generated catalog and family slots own them: `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json`, `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json`, generated `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4) |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry packages, Sentry shared helper, pino-style logger | [code] (package.json; apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts; apps/web/lib/logger.ts) |
| Hosting | Vercel (`vercel.json`: build via `apps/web/scripts/build-with-chat.sh`, cron list, git auto-deploy disabled); also a container build `apps/web/Dockerfile` (standalone output, node 24) | [code] (vercel.json:3,9-11; apps/web/Dockerfile) |
| Tests | Vitest 5 (jsdom) plus Playwright e2e | [code] (apps/web/vitest.config.ts; package.json) |

**Chat turn path (managed Cloud).** The client calls `POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions`. The route runs an auth gate (`lib/auth-gate.ts`), the managed-compute kill switch, workspace policy gates, spend limits, and then dispatches through the shared provider adapters; usage is accounted in `managed-usage-accounting-service`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:40; lib/auth-gate.ts; apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts; apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-accounting-service.ts). See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for the full pipeline.

**Public API.** The same adapters back a public OpenAI-compatible v1 route. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Provider strategy')

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Provider.** Clerk, accessed only through the identity port `getIdentityProvider()` so the provider can be swapped by environment plus one adapter. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts:11-24; packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:9-11; adapters `clerk.ts`, `clerk-sessions.ts`)

**Web sign-in screens.** `app/login` (combined log-in or sign-up entry `AuthEntryScreen.tsx`), `app/signup` (with `TermsGate`), `app/auth/*` (callback, sso-callback, reset-password, update-password, desktop, device, chrome-extension). [code] (apps/web/app/login, app/signup, app/auth)

**Middleware.** `proxy.ts` takes the identity middleware from the port. Public API routes served without identity are only `/api/health`, `/api/download`, `/api/models`, `/api/waitlist/public` and the OG image. Product routes and `/api/(.*)` run through the identity session. [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:155-164, 170-200)

**How other apps sign in.**
- Browser-origin tokens: the token's authorized party (`azp`) decides the bound surface; `chrome-extension://` origins bind to `chrome`, other origins to `web`. Mobile mints tokens from a Clerk JWT template that carries a surface claim. A token with neither binds to nothing and the plan gate fails closed. [code] (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:53-67)
- Desktop (Electron) and Chrome carry a web-minted token and may refine the surface by header `x-agi-surface`. [code] (free-chat-surface-policy.ts:31-33, 97-112)
- CLI and VS Code: device code flow (`api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `/token`, `/approve`, `/refresh`) and API keys; the page `app/device-auth`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/device; apps/web/app/device-auth)
- Desktop sign-in handoff: `/api/auth/desktop/grant` and `/redeem`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop)

**Account rules checked on the chat route.** Terms version standing, adult (18+) eligibility, MFA/passkey policy, IP allow list, CSRF and rate limits are checked in the auth gate. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:5-35)

**Anonymous use.** A guest chat route (`api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest`) exists with bot challenge, per-device and per-IP daily caps (defaults 20 and 100 messages) and spend caps; it is available only when bot protection is ready and the flag `guest.chat` is enabled. [code] (apps/web/lib/guest-chat/config.ts:3-30; guest-chat-access.ts:15-33)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The product names three modes. Here is what the web app does with each. Implementation status is separate from verification status; no run is recorded in the documents read, so every row is unverified by execution.

| Mode | Web in a plain browser | Web inside the Electron desktop host | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:cloud (managed Cloud) | Supported and the only inference path. Free and all paid plans can use managed chat. | Same hosted UI | [code] (billing-catalog.ts:346 `managed_chat: CLOUD_CHAT_TIERS`; free-chat-surface-policy.ts:97-112 maps `web` to `managed_chat`) |
| mode:local | Not supported. Local calls need the desktop host bridge; with no bridge `startLocalChat` throws `DesktopHostUnavailable`. | Supported through the host bridge (`local_chat_start`) to local model servers; text only, attachments refused; a chat that holds local turns cannot continue on a cloud model | [code] (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/runtime-client.ts:621-646; apps/web/features/chat/lib/local-turn.ts:15-70) |
| mode:own-key (BYOK) | Not supported. Web never stores a provider key; BYOK belongs to the CLI and VS Code. | Same: Desktop chat takes no provider keys | [code] (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:224); [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:44 'Must not: expose BYOK/free env-key chat or pretend Local compute is available in-browser without a connected host') |

**Local to own-key crossing.** Web contains the handoff dialog and preview logic for a Local conversation moving to a BYOK model as an explicit fork (`routeLocalToByokSend`, `LocalByokHandoffDialog`). This is code for the consent step; it does not mean web holds keys. [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:81-103; WebChatPage.tsx:412) Whether the BYOK target is reachable from web at all is [unknown].

**Free vs subscribed on web.**
- plan:free: managed chat, tools, projects, memory, skills, cloud sync. Not included: connectors, remote control, AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API, developer surfaces. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:322-361)
- Paid plans (ids `basic`, `pro` labelled Premium, `max`, `max_15x` labelled Ultra, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`): `connectors` from all paid; `agi_work`, `deep_research`, `image_generation`, `managed_api`, `developer_surfaces` from `pro` up; `video_generation` only `max_15x` and `enterprise`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-232, 346-361)
- Plan ids `local-only` and `byok` exist as free-of-charge plan tiers; they carry no managed Cloud capability. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:168-179, 296-299)
- Paid acquisition is staged: checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time switch opens it (`AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1` forces it open). [code] (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-52; checkout route.ts:300-308) The doc says the same. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:19-24)
- Kill switch: env `AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA`; unless set to 0, false or off the gate allows managed compute; when off, chat returns 403 `public_launch_blocked`. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40,50-83)

**Subscription system.** Entitlements are resolved on the server (`lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts`, `effective-subscription-service.ts`) and returned by `api:GET /api/me`; usage accounting is in `managed-usage-accounting-service.ts` and `credit-service.ts`. Clients do not compute quotas. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:20; apps/web/lib/services); [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Data ownership across surfaces')

**Free inference pools.** `apps/web/config/free-pools.json` lists promo pools with terms review fields (`reviewedBy` is null in the first entry read). [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json:1-30)

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
Web depends on these workspace packages (from `apps/web/package.json`): `@agiworkforce/types` (contracts, billing catalog, product names), `cloud-contracts`, `local-runtime-contract`, `unified-chat`, `ui`, `design-tokens`, `i18n`, `icons`, `identity`, `data-layer`, `key-value`, `object-storage`, `observability`, `provider-protocol`, `provider-runtime`, `providers-factory`, `providers-vercel-gateway`, `routing`, `search`, `skills`, `mcp`, `apply-patch`, `artifacts`, `agent-core`, `client-runtime`, `sync`, `context`, `context-engine`, `compliance`, `utils`. [code] (apps/web/package.json:19-52)

| Shared piece | Used by | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/ui/unified-chat` | Desktop, web, Chrome, VS Code (must not assume one surface's routing or billing) | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5); [code] (WebChatPage.tsx:91,412) |
| `packages/contracts/types` billing catalog and model catalog | all apps | [code] (billing-catalog.ts) |
| Provider adapters `packages/ai/providers/*` | web API and other TS surfaces | [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Provider strategy') |
| Rust protocol types exported into `packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol` | web and others | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5) |
| Neon schema `apps/web/db/neon` | canonical for every surface | [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md 'Shared Contracts') |

**Who consumes web.** Public Electron Desktop loads the hosted web app, so a change to `apps/desktop/src` never reaches it. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5). Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome call the API. Packages must not import from apps and apps must not import other apps; `pnpm check:boundaries` enforces entrypoint use. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md; AGENTS.md section 3)

**Web-private feature code.** Many features live only under `apps/web/features` (e.g. `features/chat`, `features/billing`), as the architecture doc assigns web feature roots there. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md 'Surface Feature Roots')

sections.heading: Build, run and test
sections.markdown:
Commands come from `docs/agent-context/commands.json` (surfaces.web) and `apps/web/package.json`. They were not run for this page. [code] (docs/agent-context/commands.json:125-135)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Dev server | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web dev` |
| Build | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web build` (runs `pnpm notices` then `next build`) |
| Typecheck (web only) | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web typecheck`; whole repo `pnpm typecheck:all` |
| Unit tests | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test` (Vitest, workers set by `AGI_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`, default 2) |
| One test | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test <file-or-pattern>` |
| End to end | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test:e2e` (Playwright) |
| Lint | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web lint` (max-warnings 0) |
| Container | `docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile .` from the repo root |
| Guard chain | `pnpm check:llm-operability` (runs on pre-push) |

**Gotchas.** [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12)
- `apps/web` uses its own Vitest major; run through the package script, never the root binary.
- `tsc --noEmit` in apps/web needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` or it dies with SIGABRT.
- Guards read the working tree, so stage first, then run.
- Migrations: `pnpm db:migrate -- status`, `apply --target <env>`; production apply needs `--confirm-production`.
- On the owner's 16 GB machine, heavy jobs (builds, full suites, tsc, dev servers, browsers) must go through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`; a hook denies unwrapped ones. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md 'Delegation')

**Test layout.** `apps/web/__tests__` (proxy, security headers, trust boundary, page claims), `apps/web/app/**/*.test.ts(x)`, `apps/web/lib/**/*.test.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts`. Priority tiers `priority-level-1` and `security` resolve. [code] (ls); [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12)

[requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:23)

[code] (apps/web/app/api/version/route.ts exists)

**Paid sales.** Paid upgrades on web remain waitlist or access-code gated. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:19-24). Free managed access is documented as public alpha, enabled for signed-in users (founder decision 2026-06-27). [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:21)

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
The intended unified product is one experience across six apps over one contract layer, with Local, own-key and Cloud as separate trust boundaries. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md; ARCHITECTURE.md)

| Area | Unified intent | What web does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat UI | Shared `unified-chat` package | Uses `unified-chat` pieces but keeps a very large web-only screen, `features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx`, plus its own store `shared/stores/web-chat-store.ts` [code] |
| Modes | Local, own key, Cloud everywhere it fits | Cloud only in a browser; Local only through the Electron bridge; no own-key [code] (see Modes) |
| Local-free promise | Local inference on desktop and mobile needs no paid plan | Web itself has no local inference; the Electron-hosted web UI reaches local models through the host bridge. Whether signing in is needed for Local in that host is [unknown] |
| Plan names | One AGI Subscription | Server plan ids differ from labels: `pro` is shown as Premium, `max_15x` as Ultra [code] (billing-catalog.ts:192-206) |
| Developer work | Host-owned runtime for Desktop Code, CLI and VS Code | Web has its own cloud code sessions (`api/code/sessions`, `lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts`); the matrix marks terminal use and git as absent on web [code]; [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:414-444) |
| Screen and device tools | present on desktop | Web cannot capture the screen; terminal absent [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:344, 434) |
| Copy about other apps | One truth | Web marketing and settings copy states availability of other apps from `surface-status.ts`, so those labels must be edited there [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts) |

Web is also the policy owner for entitlements, usage and moderation for all apps, so it carries server logic the other apps only consume. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services)

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Largest known gaps, each with its basis.

1. **Open Web defects.** `audit/registers/known-flaws.md` has a Web section with many rows, mostly account and workspace erasure, export and session revocation (several rated High, for example WEB-WORKSPACE-DELETION-LIFECYCLE-01, WEB-WORKSPACE-ERASURE-LOCKDOWN-01, WEB-ACCOUNT-EXPORT-ERASURE-CUSTODY-01, WEB-SESSION-REVOCATION-CLASSIFICATION-01). Most say 'runtime acceptance open'. [requirement] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md:15-40)
2. **Nothing recorded as run.** The feature matrix says no cell was produced by running the feature; whether the release workflow has ever run is not in the tree. [requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:7-13, 23)
3. **No browser Local, no own-key.** By design in the browser; users wanting Local or BYOK must use CLI, VS Code or the desktop host. [code] (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:224)
4. **Large chat files.** The large-file path (up to 500 MiB) is built but was off when documented: `CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED` unset, scanner protocol not live. Current state is [unknown] (the doc date is 2026-11-15, the migration ledger is now 425). [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md 'Chat File Uploads')
5. **Paid acquisition gated.** Waitlist or access code required unless the switch is open. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts)
6. **Free pool terms.** The first pool entry in `free-pools.json` has `reviewedBy` and `verifiedAtMs` null and an expiry timestamp, so its terms review is not recorded there. [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json)
7. **Web size.** Many routes and features in one app (88 API folders, 164 e2e specs, 577 migration-folder entries); a single chat screen file holds most chat logic. [inferred] (folder counts; WebChatPage.tsx imports)
8. **Matrix cells unverified for web:** Chat, Library, Search, slash commands, attachments and repository context are marked unverified by the matrix generator (a limit of its import search, not a proven absence). [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:44-60, 154, 194, 214, 334, 424)

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Nothing below was run for this page. [unknown] for outcomes.

1. Read the surface label: `apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts` (`SURFACE_STATUS`).
2. Check what production serves: call `GET /api/version` on the production origin and compare with main; the scheduled workflow `production-drift` does this daily. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:30-50)
3. Run web unit tests: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test`; trust boundary specifically: `apps/web/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts`; page claims: `apps/web/__tests__/surface-page-claims.test.ts`; proxy rules: `apps/web/__tests__/proxy-*.test.ts`.
4. Run e2e: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test:e2e` (specs in `apps/web/e2e`, e.g. `chat-functional-conversations.spec.ts`, `checkout.spec.ts`, `e10-desktop-login.spec.ts`).
5. Check plan gating: read `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts` and its test `packages/contracts/types/src/__tests__/billing-catalog.test.ts`.
6. Check applied migrations: `pnpm db:migrate -- status` and `scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json`.
7. Run the guard chain: `pnpm check:llm-operability` after staging changes.
8. For human-level proof, drive the built app (not `next dev`) with a test account and look at Free and subscribed states; the project asks for this rather than relying on tests alone. [requirement] (owner guidance in project memory; AGENTS.md section 12 'say what you ran')

key_facts.fact: apps/web is both the Next.js web app and the server API that all other apps and third parties call.
Stack is Next.js 16 App Router with React 19; routing middleware is proxy.ts exporting proxy, not middleware.ts.
Sign-in uses Clerk behind an identity port; default provider is clerk, selected by env AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER.

A verified token is bound to a surface from signed claims: chrome-extension origin to chrome, other origins to web, mobile via JWT template claim; no claim means unbound and the plan gate fails closed.
Web chat is managed Cloud only for all signed-in tiers including free; managed_chat capability is granted to free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise.
Web never stores a provider key; own-key (BYOK) belongs to the CLI and VS Code.
Local model chat from web works only when the Electron desktop host bridge exists; without it startLocalChat throws DesktopHostUnavailable. Local turns are text only.
Plan ids differ from display labels: pro is labelled Premium, max_15x is labelled Ultra; local-only and byok plan ids exist and are free.
Capability tiers: connectors from any paid plan; agi_work, deep_research, image_generation, managed_api, developer_surfaces from pro up; video_generation only max_15x and enterprise.
Paid checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time flag opens upgrades or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1.
Env AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA acts as an incident kill switch: only values 0, false or off block managed compute with 403 public_launch_blocked.

A guest chat route exists (POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest) with defaults of 20 messages per device and 100 per IP per day; it is on only when bot protection is ready and flag guest.chat is enabled.
Only /api/health, /api/download, /api/models, /api/waitlist/public and the OG image are served without identity.
Website surface labels mark Web 'Available now' and Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome 'Coming soon'.
Hosting is Vercel with git auto-deploy disabled; a container build via apps/web/Dockerfile also exists; deploy workflow runs after CI and has a daily drift alarm and a rollback input.
Committed migration ledger says production migrations applied through 425 as of 2026-11-21.
Chat screen mount chain is app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx to WebChatRoot to WebChatPage.
Public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so apps/desktop/src changes never reach it.
Web test commands: pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test (Vitest, jsdom), test:e2e (Playwright); typecheck needs 8 GB heap; web uses its own Vitest major.

apps/web/db/neon is an append-only checksummed migration chain; tables seen include profiles, subscriptions, conversations, messages, usage_events, media_assets, chat_file_intakes, feature_flag_definitions, feature_flags, beta_invites, beta_redemptions, api_keys, organizations.
Entitlements, quota and plan values are computed on the server and returned by GET /api/me; clients never compute them.
Open Web defects are tracked in audit/registers/known-flaws.md (Web section), many rated High on erasure, export and session revocation, with runtime acceptance open.
No document in the tree records a real run of the web release or features; feature-matrix 'Present' means located, not exercised.
Large chat file path (up to 500 MiB) was built but gated off (CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED unset) when documented on 2026-11-15.
Model identifiers are not written in web code; the catalog files own them.

open_questions: Is web chat currently serving production users, and at which commit? Only GET /api/version or the deploy workflow run history can say; the tree records no run.
Does the Electron-hosted web UI require sign-in for Local chat? The web code reaches local models through the host bridge but the sign-in requirement for that path was not traced.
Can a BYOK target ever be reached from web? The handoff dialog exists in web but no web key storage was found.
Is CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED on in production now, and is the scanner at protocol 2? Documented as off on 2026-11-15; ledger has since advanced to migration 425.
Has the first free-pool entry in apps/web/config/free-pools.json been reviewed? Its reviewedBy and verifiedAtMs are null.
Product choice left open: when to open paid acquisition on web to everyone (the waitlist switch is a run-time flag).
Whether the guest chat flag guest.chat is on in production is unknown.
Which of the surface-feature-matrix 'Unverified' web cells (Chat, Library, Search) are truly absent or only missed by its import search was not settled.
